clue.text: Very warm keeping distance, almost very cold being instructive

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: very warm weather or food is hot
a mile is a measure of distance

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: very cold means icy

explanation.surface: A weather report swinging from heat to freezing at a distance turns out to be educational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' and 'almost' are the two signals: a short trim on the cold word, and a measure of distance held inside the warm one.
explanation.definitionFit: Homiletic means of or like a sermon, preaching moral instruction, hence instructive.

clue.text: Brought before the bench, end of which said to make sense

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: which refers back to the bench just named

indicators.note: said means the following is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: to add up is to make sense

explanation.surface: Hauled before the magistrates, where the end of it all is supposed to be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' stands for 'bench', whose end is H; 'said' gives ADUP for a spoken 'add up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had up is to be charged and summoned to appear in court.

clue.text: Err in interpreting lost letter from novelist of village life

indicators.note: one letter of the name goes missing

parts.note: Miss Read, pen name of Dora Saint, wrote gentle novels of English village life

explanation.surface: A novelist of rural England loses a letter and gets the wrong end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Read wrote the Fairacre books about an English village; one S goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To misread is to take something the wrong way, a mistaken interpretation.

clue.text: Then are cats heard to soar in 14 down?

definitions.text: Then are cats heard to soar in 14 down?

parts.words: Then are cats heard to soar in 14 down?
parts.note: a riddle swapping the usual pairing of cats that purr and birds that soar: if the singing birds purred, cats would soar; say that idea aloud for a garden plant

explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a tall delphinium-like garden plant with spurred flowers, at home in a flower border.

clue.text: Food for friar

definitions.meaning: slang for food, as in a school ... shop
Friar ... of the Robin Hood legend

explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British slang for snacks and sweets, and Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's jovial companion.

clue.text: Outlaw civil analyst in exchange for heating aid

indicators.note: exchange means the letters are swapped around

explanation.surface: Trade a lawless analyst for something that keeps the house warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling the gap between a wall's two skins keeps heat in, helping a home stay warm.

clue.text: I faint without love, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the next word wraps round the following one

parts.note: faint light is dim
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone swoons for lack of love, or so the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting O inside DIM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression, a particular way of speaking peculiar to a language.

clue.text: See 5
Concentrated in Tennessee, so to speak

indicators.note: the state's name is said aloud and spelt as the sounds it is made of

parts.note: spoken, the state's name runs like ten-ess-ee

explanation.surface: A concentration in the state of Tennessee, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Tennessee' as TEN, the letter S and the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong and focused, as a concentrated flavour is.

clue.text: One of seven Taliban leaders imprisoned by Egyptian leader at Pole

indicators.note: being imprisoned by something means being shut inside it

parts.note: Mohamed Morsi, president of Egypt when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word, here its first three

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Taliban chiefs locked up by Egypt's president at the Pole: one of seven wrongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes TAL, the first three letters of Taliban.
explanation.definitionFit: Christianity lists seven deadly sins; a mortal sin is a grave one of that kind.

clue.text: Exact number: is it held by Christian social worker?

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer
exact means strict
V is five in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether an exact figure is kept by a Christian charity worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks religious but is the couturier's first name; 'held by' puts the rest inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A district visitor was a parish volunteer who called on the poor and sick, an early welfare role.

clue.text: Remove protection from 18

definitions.meaning: to strip off a skin or rind
a town on the island in 18 across, the Isle of Man

explanation.definitionFit: Peeling removes a protective skin, and Peel is a west-coast town on the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Fast girl first in Georgian city

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia
A is a first-class mark or grade

explanation.surface: A racy young woman who came first in Atlanta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' points not to the country or the era but to the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a huntress who could outrun any suitor, so a girl who was fast.

clue.text: Historical sitcom, possibly worse without something missing

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: badder is a colloquial, perhaps doubtful, comparative of bad
a lack is something missing

explanation.surface: A period comedy that could be worse if something were left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' flags BADDER as non-standard English. Blackadder is a BBC comedy set in different eras of British history.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackadder is the BBC series following generations of a scheming family through English history.

clue.text: Pray church leader with bible to give us another look

definitions.text: Pray church leader with bible to give us another look

indicators.note: giving the letters a new look means rearranging them
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A prayer that the vicar and his Bible let us watch again.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is also the definition, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC iPlayer is the BBC's online service for catching up on programmes already broadcast.

clue.text: Dishonesty at the front applied to string

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle or dishonest dealing
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Cheating up front is tied to a string, as in a con trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle bow is the horsehair stick drawn across a violin's strings to play it.

clue.text: Bottom of river at border?

parts.note: a river is a thing that flows, a flower
the bed is the bottom of a river

explanation.surface: Looking for the riverbed at a frontier crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of river' wants to be the riverbed, but the river is a flow-er.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower bed along a lawn edge or wall is called a border by gardeners.

clue.text: Lock showing tension with top removed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken off, the top in a down or across light alike

parts.note: tension means stress

explanation.surface: A lock that shows strain once the top is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock or long strand of hair.

clue.text: Shakespearean character going round without error? About right

parts.note: something round has the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next piece is put round the following one

parts.note: sic is printed after a quoted mistake to say it is reproduced as written, so wryly 'without error'

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure going about without error, about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Osric is the foppish courtier in Hamlet who referees the final duel.

clue.text: Meat wrapped by artist with most of 14 across, part 1

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the first part of 14 across is FIDDLE, another word for which is violin

explanation.surface: Meat in pastry wrapped by a painter who also plays the fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are little pasta parcels typically stuffed with minced meat.

clue.text: Article follows lives by top cat and top soldier, where house has keys

indicators.note: the article comes after the other pieces, so it goes last

parts.note: lives means is (exists)
Leo the lion, king of the beasts and so the top cat
FM is a Field Marshal, the highest army rank
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A riddle about a house whose keys go to the top cat and the top soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Keys is the elected chamber of the Isle of Man's parliament, Tynwald, so 'house has keys' is no locksmith joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's lower house of parliament is called the House of Keys.

clue.text: Scottish island, one — nearly one — in part of window

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish island, one or so, in part of a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullion is the vertical bar dividing the lights of a window.

clue.text: Quarters that can survive — that one wishes one had

parts.note: E and N are two quarters, or points, of the compass
viable means able to live or survive

explanation.surface: Living quarters that last are something to covet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enviable arouses envy, a desire to own it oneself.

clue.text: Dessert cooked by tramp last month

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up as in a recipe

parts.note: ult., ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A pudding made by a vagrant last month.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT is old commercial shorthand for last month, ultimo.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie or flan with plums is a classic pudding.

clue.text: Volcanic stuff in periodical, most of it

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: it refers back to the periodical, a mag

explanation.surface: Hot rock features in a magazine, filling most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the periodical again, MAG, of which 'most' is MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is the molten rock beneath the earth's crust that erupts as lava.

clue.text: See 3
See 21
Having a strong local accent? More or less

explanation.definitionFit: Broad speech is heavy regional dialect; the set phrase also means generally or approximately.

clue.text: Dormice are oddly more dehydrated

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Sleepy rodents are, strangely, even thirstier.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier is the comparative of dry, which means lacking water.

clue.text: "Land of Hope" formed aria — run it

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A patriotic song title is turned into a tune to be run through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Hope' sounds like the patriotic anthem, but means the country Anthony Hope invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.
